content_list.content_text: Hollywood musicals are deeply associated with the golden age of American cinema, but they did not disappear with the end of the studio system. Instead, they changed shape. The traditional musical could still be found often, slightly reworked to suit a more modern audience.

information.contentText: The disco where Tony Manero shines - 2001 Odyssey (inspired by Stanley Kubrick's 1968 film "2001: A Space Odyssey"), in Brooklyn - operated as such until 1987, when it became a gay club called Spectrum. In 2005, despite protests from the film's fans, who regarded the place as a shrine, the venue was demolished.

content_list.content_text: However, the genre was taken into new areas, exploring contemporary issues and fads, as a platform for new musical genres or to reassess the past. The first two installments, That's Entertainment! (1974) and That's Entertainment, Part II (1976), recalled the heyday of the Hollywood musical.

There were also contemporary releases that differed little from 1950s productions: Scrooge (1970), Willy Wonka & the Chocolate Factory (1971), Fiddler on the Roof (1971), Funny Lady (1975) and Annie (1982) adopted a classic style and offered a perfect escape from reality.

information.contentText: In the traditional form of musical theater, every significant character in the stage version sings to express their own emotions and to advance the plot. In the film version, the musical numbers are entirely diegetic, usually sung in the Kit Kat Klub itself, with one exception ("Tomorrow Belongs to Me").

content_list.content_text: Nevertheless, Norman Jewison (b. 1926) gave an inventive spin to Jesus Christ Superstar (1973), which featured songs by the new wunderkinds of musical theater, Andrew Lloyd Webber and Tim Rice. That same year, another reinterpretation of a biblical story, Godspell, also appeared.

content_list.title: Cabaret: The Political, Modern Musical
content_list.description:
Bob Fosse's masterpiece is a cynical critique of the last decadent days of the Weimar Republic, on the eve of the rise of National Socialism, with frivolous, catchy songs that mask the troubling events unfolding in Europe.

Brian (Michael York) arrives in Berlin in 1931. He meets Sally Bowles (Liza Minnelli) and the two become lovers. She works at the Kit Kat Klub (note the three Ks), an underground cabaret cut off from the outside world. Sally and Brian's fleeting affair is put into perspective by the violent turmoil surrounding them, which begins to destroy the freedoms they cherish so much.

Glimpses of Nazi brutality go unnoticed by those enjoying themselves at the cabaret. The songs bring the plot and characters to life, driving the narrative while also commenting on the unfolding events. "Maybe This Time" expresses Sally's high hopes; "If You Could See Her" is a terrifying allegory of the intense persecution of Berlin's Jewish population. The songs are performed on the stage of the Kit Kat Klub and, apart from the expressionist angles revealing morally gray spectators, the numbers are staged realistically. Fosse shows the performances from a distance, using the glare of the lights to emphasize the small stage and the silhouettes of heads in the audience - conspirators in this dark world.

The final frames repeat the opening scene, with the smeared glass reflecting those who have finally taken over the audience, identifiable only by their swastika-adorned armbands. A mirror is held up to society, and the figures in it are hazy, distorted, sharing a cruel worldview.
content_list.credits: Summary based on the text by Simon Ward, published in the book "Cinema: The Whole Story" by Philip Kemp

content_list.content_text: The counterculture born in the 1960s was equally represented by adaptations of stage shows: Oh! Calcutta! (1972) and Hair (1979). Although they adopted a conventional narrative structure, these films - like the shows they were based on - were controversial for breaking taboos regarding nudity, sex and politics.

information.contentText: The production became a reference point for artists such as Jennifer Lopez and Geri Halliwell, who, in the music videos for "I'm Glad" and "It's Raining Men," play the story's protagonist in scenes recreated for the videos.

content_list.content_text: Bob Fosse (1927-1989) was the dominant force in the American musical from the late 1960s onward. A choreographer by training, Fosse created a singular style that used every limb to accentuate a dancer's movement. His Cabaret (1972) won eight Oscars, while All That Jazz (1979), a frank, semi-autobiographical account of a director on the verge of collapse amid preparations for his next show, was awarded the Palme d'Or at the Cannes Film Festival.

Rock dominated most musicals from the 1970s onward. Alan Parker (b. 1944), who also directed Bugsy Malone (1976) and Fame (1980), directed Pink Floyd: The Wall (1982). A more traditional style was evident in Grease (1978), which casts an affectionate eye on teenage rebellion and romance and became the decade's biggest musical hit.

information.contentText: The film premiered at the Cannes Film Festival on May 12, 1987, and was released in the United States on August 21, 1987, grossing more than US$217 million worldwide.[4] It was the first film to sell more than a million copies on home video, and the soundtrack spawned several hit singles, including "(I've Had) The Time of My Life," which won the Golden Globe and the Oscar for Best Original Song, as well as a Grammy for best duet.

content_list.content_text: The Rocky Horror Picture Show (1975) combines the sexual standards that prevailed after the 1960s with a salute to the horror films of the 1940s, all driven by a series of skillfully produced musical numbers. Even the punk movement was represented - The Great Rock 'n' Roll Swindle (1980) introduced the Sex Pistols to a wider world.

quote.quote: ...In the way Saturday Night Fever has been directed and photographed, we feel the languid pull of the disco, and its garish tone is transformed. The film has some of the most hypnotic and beautiful pop dance scenes ever filmed...
quote.author: Gene Siskel on Saturday Night Fever

content_list.content_text: The success of Saturday Night Fever (1977) practically ignited the disco phenomenon, thanks to the infectious soundtrack by the Bee Gees, and spurred a series of dance films that gained popularity during the 1980s. Staying Alive (1983) saw John Travolta's (b. 1954) character, Tony Manero, attempt a career on Broadway, while in Flashdance (1983), the factory worker played by Jennifer Beals (b. 1963) dreams of getting into dance school.

content_list.title: The Rocky Horror Picture Show
content_list.description:
Richard O'Brien's offbeat stage musical, adapted for the screen in 1975, was a flop on its release. However, when a New York theater began showing it at midnight screenings, word quickly spread about the bizarre science fiction and horror spoof. The film became a cult hit and to this day holds the record for the longest theatrical run, having been shown at the same theater in Munich, Germany, every week for more than 27 years.

A very young Susan Sarandon (b. 1946) and Barry Bostwick (b. 1945) star as Janet and Brad, an innocent couple whose car breaks down on a stormy night, forcing them to seek shelter in a nearby castle, unaware that it belongs to the stockings-and-garters-clad transvestite Frank N. Furter (Tim Curry, reprising his stage role) and his friends from Transylvania, including the sinister Riff Raff (Richard O'Brien) and Magenta (Patricia Quinn). Also living in the mansion are the biker Eddie (Meat Loaf), a failed creation (in the style of Frankenstein's monster) of Frank N. Furter, and Rocky (Peter Hinwood), his perfectly tanned replacement/upgrade.

Narrated by Dr. Everett Scott (Jonathan Adams) and driven by glam rock, the film is a celebration of sexuality: Frank N. Furter and his troupe try to seduce the virginal Brad and Janet to the tune of memorable songs such as "Touch-a Touch-a Touch Me", "Sweet Transvestite" and, of course, "Time Warp". The mix of brazen sexuality, ironic quips, outrageous costumes, and double entendres is unlike anything ever done in cinema. It is easy to see why the catchy songs and highly quotable dialogue became such a huge hit with fans, the most enthusiastic of whom dress up as the characters, act out parts of the film during screenings, and bring props to use at specific moments in the film, for example, throwing rice during the wedding scene. The Rocky Horror Picture Show may not be a film for the whole family, but it is still fantastic kitsch fun.
content_list.credits: Summary based on the text by Joanna Berry, published in the book 1001 Movies You Must See Before You Die

information.contentTitle: Scenes from The Rocky Horror Picture Show
information.contentText: The central theme of RHPS (as fans also call the film) is its satire of horror and science fiction films and series. This can be seen in everything from the idea of a scientist who tries to create a man in a laboratory doing so out of sexual desire, to the explicit references to characters such as Flash Gordon and to the studios that made such films, such as RKO Pictures.

content_list.content_text: Conservatism stood against dancing in two of the decade's most popular musicals, Footloose (1984) and Dirty Dancing (1987). As in all 1980s musicals, the music was prerecorded and generally included tracks familiar to audiences, boosting their popularity.
content_list.content_credits: Summary based on the text by Ian Haydn Smith, published in the book "Cinema: The Whole Story" by Philip Kemp

movies.title: Cabaret
movies.overview: Inside the Kit Kat Club of 1931 Berlin, starry-eyed singer Sally Bowles and an impish emcee sound the clarion call to decadent fun, while outside a certain political party grows into a brutal force.

movies.title: The Rocky Horror Picture Show
movies.overview: Sweethearts Brad and Janet, stuck with a flat tire during a storm, discover the eerie mansion of Dr. Frank-N-Furter, a transvestite scientist. As their innocence is lost, Brad and Janet meet a houseful of wild characters, including a rocking biker and a creepy butler. Through elaborate dances and rock songs, Frank-N-Furter unveils his latest creation: a muscular man named 'Rocky'.

movies.title: Saturday Night Fever
movies.overview: Tony Manero is a Brooklyn paint-store clerk who'd give anything to break out of his dead-end existence. In life, Tony is a peasant; on the disco dance floor, he's a king. As the soundtrack plays one Bee Gees hit after another, white-suited Tony struts his stuff amidst flashing lights and sweaty, undulating bodies. Tony's class aspirations are mirrored in his relationship with his dance partner, a secretary eager to move into the glamorous world of Manhattan.

movies.title: Dirty Dancing
movies.overview: Expecting the usual tedium that accompanies a summer in the Catskills with her family, 17-year-old Frances 'Baby' Houseman is surprised to find herself stepping into the shoes of a professional hoofer—and unexpectedly falling in love.

movies.title: Flashdance
movies.overview: The popular 1980s dance movie that depicts the life of an exotic dancer with a side job as a welder whose true desire is to get into ballet school. It’s her dream to be a professional dancer and now is her chance.

movies.title: Willy Wonka & the Chocolate Factory
movies.overview: Eccentric candy man Willy Wonka prompts a worldwide frenzy when he announces that golden tickets hidden inside five of his delicious candy bars will admit their lucky holders into his top-secret confectionary. But does Wonka have an agenda hidden amid a world of Oompa Loompas and chocolate rivers?

movies.title: Grease
movies.overview: Australian good girl Sandy and greaser Danny fell in love over the summer. But when they unexpectedly discover they're now in the same high school, will they be able to rekindle their romance despite their eccentric friends?

movies.title: Hair
movies.overview: "Hair" is a 1979 musical war comedy-drama film adaptation of the 1968 Broadway musical "Hair: An American Tribal Love-Rock Musical" about a Vietnam War draftee, Claude, who meets and befriends a tribe of long-haired hippies on his way to the army induction center.  Claude heads to New York upon receiving his draft notice, leaving the family ranch in Oklahoma. He arrives in New York where he is rapidly indoctrinated into the youth subculture before reporting in for boot camp.

movies.title: Funny Lady
movies.overview: 1930s in New York – The famous singer Fanny Brice has divorced her first husband Nicky Arnstein. During the depression she has trouble finding work as an artist but meets Billy Rose, a newcomer who writes lyrics and owns his own nightclub.

movies.title: Jesus Christ Superstar
movies.overview: Oscar-nominated film adaptation of the rock opera of the same name, based on the last weeks before the crucifixion of Jesus. The film was directed by Norman Jewison. Ted Neeley and Carl Anderson were nominated for two 1974 Golden Globe Award for their portrayals of Jesus and Judas, respectively.

movies.title: All That Jazz
movies.overview: Joe Gideon is at the top of the heap, one of the most successful directors and choreographers in musical theater. But he can feel his world slowly collapsing around him - his obsession with work has almost destroyed his personal life, and only his bottles of pills keep him going.

movies.name: Fame
movies.overview:
Fame is an American television series originally produced between 1982 and 1987. The show is based on the 1980 motion picture of the same name. Using a mixture of drama and music, it followed the lives of the students and faculty at the New York City High School for the Performing Arts. Although fictional, it was based heavily on the actual Fiorello H. LaGuardia High School of Music & Art and Performing Arts in New York. Most interior scenes were filmed in Hollywood, California. In all seasons except the 3rd, the show filmed several exterior scenes on location in New York City.

The popularity of the series, particularly in the UK, led to several hit records and live concert tours by the cast. Despite its success, very few of the actors maintained high-profile careers after the series was cancelled. A number of the cast members were seen again briefly in Bring Back...Fame, a reunion special made for UK television in 2008.

movies.title: Pink Floyd: The Wall
movies.overview: A troubled rock star descends into madness in the midst of his physical and social isolation from everyone.

content_list.title: Timeline of Events from 1970 to 1989
content_list.description: The Exorcist is released, making audiences around the world sick and causing them to faint, creating a global hysteria. The first blockbuster is released: Jaws; meanwhile, auteur cinema grows with Martin Scorsese and other great directors. The '80s arrive with low-budget productions and era-defining comedies.
